subject: Post-call recap: pilot goals, integration constraints, and next ops
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily@truhealth.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: pilot goals, integration constraints, and next ops

Hi Emily — thanks again for the call today. Quick written recap so we have a shared view and clear next steps. Appreciate you looping Jordan (platform) and sharing the procurement timeline.

Key pain points you described
- Latency sensitivity on triage flow: <200ms p50 for short prompts (20-60 tokens) and p95 < 700ms.
- Cost predictability: want an expected cost-per-session target to evaluate economics across 5M monthly queries.
- Safety/regulatory: PHI in some inputs; must meet SOC2 controls and support VPC/private control plane for the pilot.

Pilot goals (MVP)
1) Launch a 6-week pilot that replaces your current triage LLM for initial symptom extraction and recommended next-step ranking.
2) Validate throughput (10–15 req/s sustained, burst to 40) and latency SLOs above.
3) Evaluate embeddings + reranking for structured recommendations (expected improvement in top-1 accuracy).

Integration & product fit notes (what we discussed)
- SDK/tech changes: Redwood client supports both streaming token-by-token and single-shot JSON outputs. For your use case we recommend:
  * Streaming for the triage UX path (low-latency first-token visibility).
  * Structured outputs using our schema-enforced JSON output to normalize symptom entities.
- Function calling: we propose using a simple Call/Invoke shim where Redwood returns a structured function payload (name + args) that your backend will map to business logic.
- Embeddings + rerank: generate dense vectors from candidate responses, use a rerank step in Redwood or in your infra. We'll demo both.
- KV/prefix cache: enable request-level KV cache for repeat prompts in the same session to reduce token costs.

Technical constraints you mentioned
- On-prem connector required for PHI subset (pilot needs hybrid routing: non-PHI to hosted, PHI to private cluster).
- Minimum TLS mutual-auth and KMS integration for keys.
- Procurement requires SOC2 evidence and a short SOW with clearly defined SLAs.

Proposed next steps (owners & timing)
1) Karthik: Share a 1-page pilot SOW + integration checklist by EOD Wed (attached).
2) Jordan: Provide expected SDK changes and code samples for function-calling mapping by Fri.
3) Grace: Prepare a brief security package (SOC2 cert, KMS integration notes, data flow diagram) and the security questionnaire responses by Mon.
4) Emily / TruHealth: Confirm pilot scope (PHI vs non-PHI split) and procurement contact; propose kickoff date window (wk of Sep 6).

Attachments:
- pilot_sow_draft_v1.pdf (attachment stub)
- integration_checklist.xlsx (attachment stub)

Thanks — I'll follow up with the SOW + checklist. If any of this is misaligned, flag it and I will revise.

Best,
Karthik Iyer

Emily / team — quick technical follow-up from our side on the hybrid routing and SDK integration: 

- Private cluster: We will provide a VPC-deployable package that exposes an internal inference endpoint. That endpoint can be fronted by your ALB/NLB; mutual TLS is supported.
- Data residency: PHI logs can be written to a customer-managed S3 bucket (encrypted with your KMS). Redwood control plane only stores audit metadata (no PHI).
- SDK changes: two small helpers we'll add to the SDK repo for the pilot:
  1) function_call_mapper: translates Redwood structured JSON "calls" into your internal function signatures (examples included).
  2) streaming_adapter: a light shim that converts partial token streams into your existing websocket UX.
- Resource sizing: For the pilot target (20 req/s peak, p95 < 700ms), we recommend a single 8-GPU private pool (A100 equivalent) with autoscale policy to +1 node for bursts.

I'll attach a minimal architecture diagram and code snippet. Jordan will add a short sample repo with the function_call_mapper by EOD.

Grace O'Connor
